notes: FDA approved 2015 as Imlygic; BioVex acquired by Amgen 2011. OncoVEX GM-CSF was the BioVex-era development name. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).

Conditionally approved in Japan 2021 as Delytact. No human transgene (LacZ marker in ICP6); targets left empty. Wikidata has a duplicate item Q110220405 (carries the UNII) beside Q116044341 (the English Wikipedia item).

platform: adenovirus (Ad5, E1B-55kDa and partial E3 deleted)
notes: Approved in China 2005 as Oncorine; no INN, so the code H101 is the preferred name. Construct description not re-verified from a primary source.
Unmodified wild-type reovirus isolate; no transgenes.

originator: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
notes: Originated at MD Anderson as Delta-24-RGD, licensed to and renamed DNX-2401 by DNAtrix. A separate NCIt concept (C159798) covers MSC-delivered DNX-2401, which is a delivery form, not a separate construct.

Cell Genesys -> BioSante (2009 merger) -> Cold Genesys (acquired asset 2010); Cold Genesys renamed CG Oncology in March 2020. Kissei holds Japan/Asia rights (2020). Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).
Transgenes are trimerized membrane-bound CD40L and 4-1BBL, per the NCIt synonym; HGNC symbols assigned by the curator. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).

Transgene is human PH20 hyaluronidase; HGNC symbol for PH20 is SPAM1 (curator mapping). VCN Biosciences spun out of ICO-IDIBELL and was acquired by Synthetic Biologics in 2022, which renamed itself Theriva Biologics. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).
Construct name Ad5/3-E2F-d24-hTNFa-IRES-hIL2 from NCIt; transgenes TNF-alpha and IL-2. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).

FDA accelerated approval 6 Aug 2026 as Tudriqev (vusolimogene oderparepvec-wtpg), with nivolumab, in advanced melanoma. Second transgene is a gibbon ape leukaemia virus envelope glycoprotein (GALV-GP R-), which is viral, so not in targets. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).

Jennerex acquired by SillaJen in 2014; Transgene was a partner and used the code TG-6006. Not the same product as TG6002, a different Transgene vaccinia construct. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).

Unarmed backbone; selected by directed evolution and first called ColoAd1. PsiOxus renamed itself Akamis Bio in January 2023. The armed T-SIGn vectors NG-350A and NG-641 are separate constructs, so separate programs (not entered here).
Lentiviral anti-CD19 (FMC63) 4-1BB CAR. CART-19 also used generically for other CD19 CARs (ambiguous).
Gammaretroviral anti-CD19 (FMC63) CD28 CAR from NCI Surgery Branch, licensed to Kite. Same CAR as brexucabtagene autoleucel; different manufacturing.
Same CAR construct as axi-cel but T-cell-enriched manufacturing; separate INN, so separate program.
Lentiviral anti-CD19 4-1BB CAR with EGFRt, defined CD4:CD8 composition. Juno acquired by Celgene, then BMS.
Anti-BCMA 4-1BB CAR; co-developed by bluebird bio (later 2seventy bio) and Celgene/BMS.
Bi-epitopic anti-BCMA VHH CAR. LCAR-B38M (Legend, China) and JNJ-68284528 treated as one product.
Fast-off-rate anti-CD19 (CAT19) 4-1BB CAR from UCL (Pule lab), developed by UCL spin-out Autolus.
Same CD19 CAR construct as liso-cel, but JW's own process (no separate CD4/CD8 trains); separate INN, so separate program.
Fully human anti-BCMA scFv CAR; co-developed by IASO Bio and Innovent (IBI326). Approved in China 2023.
Anti-BCMA CAR with synthetic D-domain binder. Gilead acquired Arcellx in 2026; BLA under FDA review (PDUFA 2026-12-23).
KRAS G12C (OFF-state covalent). Approved (US 2021 Lumakras; EU Lumykras).
KRAS G12C (OFF-state covalent). Mirati acquired by BMS Jan 2024. Approved (Krazati).
KRAS G12C covalent. Roche code RG6330. UNII is free base; adipate salt is separate NCIt C203123 / UNII OA9191WV3C.

KRAS G12D non-covalent. No INN found. BMS reported discontinued (ApexOnco 2025-03-05). Reported discontinued by Bristol Myers Squibb (ApexOnco, 2025-03-05); kept because trials and papers use the name.
Multi-selective RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor. FDA approved 2026-08-26 as Rasonque (pancreatic cancer).
KRAS G12C(ON) covalent tri-complex inhibitor. Wikidata QID not confirmed.
KRAS G12D(ON) covalent tri-complex inhibitor. NCIt also lists RM-036 (unverified elsewhere).

sponsor: Jacobio Pharmaceuticals; Shanghai Allist Pharmaceuticals (Greater China)
notes: KRAS G12C. Approved China (NMPA, May 2025) as 艾瑞凯; China rights licensed to Allist 2024. Wikidata QID not confirmed.
KRAS G12C. GenFleet code GFH925; Innovent code IBI351 after Sept 2021 China licence. Approved China Aug 2024 as Dupert. Wikidata QID not confirmed.
KRAS G12C covalent (second generation).

platform: adenovirus (Ad2/Ad5 chimera, E1B-55kDa and E3 deleted)
notes: First engineered oncolytic virus in human trials (1996). Development as ONYX-015 was stopped by Onyx/Pfizer in 2003; the closely related Chinese construct H101 (AXP000003) was approved instead. INN lontucirev is rarely used; ONYX-015 is the common name.

Telomelysin/OBP-301. Telomerase (hTERT) promoter drives E1A and E1B via an IRES. Partnered with Chugai (Japan) and with Merck/Roche in combination studies at various times; partnership history not re-verified.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5/3 chimera, Delta-24, E3 gp19k/6.7k replaced by GM-CSF)
notes: Development code CGTG-102; the same construct was given to ATAP patients in Finland as Ad5/3-D24-GMCSF before Oncos Therapeutics was formed. Oncos Therapeutics merged with Targovax in 2015. Targovax deprioritised its oncolytic adenovirus programme around 2022-2023; current status not confirmed from a primary source.

originator: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
notes: DNX-2440: DNX-2401 (AXP000005) backbone armed with OX40L, so a separate program under SPEC section 1. Trials in glioblastoma (NCT03714334) and, by superselective intra-arterial infusion, in liver metastases (NCT04714983).

platform: adenovirus (Ad5 Delta-24-RGD with T1 E3/19K mutation)
notes: Delta-24-RGD backbone plus the T1 mutation (single adenine insertion in E3/19K) that increases virus release. Phase I/IIa in prostate cancer, NCT04097002.

platform: adenovirus (Ad11p/Ad3 group B chimera, T-SIGn vector)
notes: Enadenotucirev (AXP000012) backbone armed with a full-length agonistic anti-CD40 antibody; separate construct, separate program. PsiOxus renamed itself Akamis Bio in January 2023.

platform: adenovirus (Ad11p/Ad3 group B chimera, T-SIGn vector)
notes: Enadenotucirev backbone armed with a FAP/CD3 bispecific T-cell activator (FAP-TAc) plus CXCL9, CXCL10 and interferon alpha.
Oncolytic adenovirus carrying a TGF-beta trap transgene. Phase I/II BETA PRIME, NCT04673942, intratumoral, alone and with a checkpoint inhibitor.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5, IFN-beta and chimeric CD40 ligand-armed)
notes: Conditionally replicating adenovirus encoding human IFN-beta and a chimeric membrane-stable CD40 ligand (MEM40). Phase I NCT05076760, intratumoral, with nivolumab.

Oncolytic adenovirus engineered to express IL-12 and an anti-PD-L1 mini-antibody, given intratumorally and followed by autologous HER2-specific CAR T cells (NCT03740256). The CAR T product is a separate program, not entered here.
Korean oncolytic adenovirus; phase I/II NCT06265025, intratumoral, alone and with pembrolizumab. Transgenes and backbone not stated in any source consulted; left empty rather than guessed.

Recombinant oncolytic adenovirus expressing an interferon ('L-IFN'), described by its developers as cancer-targeting gene-virotherapy (CTGVT). Trials NCT05180851, NCT05914935. Originator company name taken from the product code, not from a primary source.

Oncolytic adenovirus with a synthetic gene circuit that restricts replication and GM-CSF expression to alpha-fetoprotein-positive cancer cells. Phase I NCT04612504 in AFP-positive hepatocellular carcinoma.

Also written Ad-TD-nsIL12 / Ad5-TD-nsIL-12. The academic trials run by Capital Medical University (NCT05717712, NCT05717699) and the company trials of BioTTT001 appear to be the same construct; merged here on the strength of the NCIt synonym Ad5-TD-nsIL-12. Worth a curator check.

Second-generation Henry Ford construct: yeast cytosine deaminase/mutant HSV-1 thymidine kinase (SR39) fusion suicide gene plus restored adenovirus death protein, used with 5-FC and valganciclovir and with radiotherapy. Trials in prostate cancer, pancreatic cancer and brain metastases (NCT03029871, NCT05686798).
Third-generation Henry Ford construct: the suicide-gene fusion plus human IL-12. Phase I trials in prostate cancer (NCT02555397) and metastatic pancreatic cancer (NCT03281382).

First-generation Henry Ford replication-competent adenovirus carrying a cytosine deaminase/HSV-1 thymidine kinase fusion gene, given intraprostatically with 5-FC/ganciclovir and radiotherapy from 1999. Construct details not re-verified against the primary trial report.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5, E2F-1 promoter-driven E1A-Delta24, RGD fiber)
notes: Given both naked (phase I melanoma, NCT01864759) and carried in bone-marrow mesenchymal stromal cells as Celyvir (autologous, NCT01844661) and AloCELYVIR (allogeneic, NCT04758533). Treated here as one program with a carrier, not three; a curator may prefer to split the cell products out.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5, modified E2F-1 promoter with extra E2F sites, Delta-24, RGD fiber)
notes: Given to 21 patients with advanced solid tumours in Finland under the Advanced Therapy Access Program (ATAP), an individualised-treatment programme rather than a registered clinical trial (Nokisalmi et al., Clin Cancer Res 2010). No registered trial found.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5, survivin promoter-driven E1A, polylysine (pk7) fiber)
notes: Delivered in HB1.F3.CD neural stem cells (NSC-CRAd-S-pk7) into the resection cavity in newly diagnosed malignant glioma, NCT03072134.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5, rat probasin promoter-E1A, PSA promoter-E1B, E3 retained)
notes: Formerly CV787. Intraprostatic phase I and intravenous phase I/II (NCT00103428 with docetaxel, NCT00116155) in hormone-refractory prostate cancer. Discontinued; Cell Genesys merged into BioSante in 2009.
Formerly CV706. Phase I of intraprostatic injection in locally recurrent prostate cancer after radiotherapy (DeWeese et al., Cancer Res 2001, PMID 11454691). Discontinued.
First patient dosed July 2023 in phase 1 NCT05904236; given intratumorally and intravenously in advanced solid tumours. Carries a YPet reporter per NCIt.

Selected by directed evolution; replicates in cancer cells and in cancer-associated fibroblasts. First patient dosed November 2024 in the phase 1/2a OCTOPOD trial in ovarian cancer (intraperitoneal). Backbone serotype not stated in sources consulted.
Phase 1/2 NCT06549946, alone and with pembrolizumab. Described by the developer as an E1B-mutant oncolytic adenovirus; exact mutation not confirmed from a primary source.

originator: Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
sponsor: Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
notes: Recombinant oncolytic adenovirus in phase I trials in gynaecological malignancies (NCT06552598) and a second Tongji trial (NCT07359235); preclinical work also in bladder cancer. Construct not described in sources consulted.
Phase 1 in recurrent malignant glioma, NCT06585527, started August 2024. The registration gives no construct description; nothing entered that could not be verified.
Oncolytic adenovirus in an early-phase trial at Zhongnan Hospital (NCT06757153). Construct, transgenes and originator not found; entered on the strength of the trial registration alone.

sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University
notes: Recombinant oncolytic adenovirus injection, NCT06632964. Construct not described in the registration.
Oncolytic adenovirus in trial NCT07697937. Construct not described; classification as an adenovirus rests on the trial's indexing and should be re-checked.
Oncolytic adenovirus, trial NCT07086105 (Australia). Construct not described in the registration.

Phase I of intratumoral injection in 27 patients with advanced solid tumours (Li et al., Gene Ther 2009;16:376-82). Sister product to H101 (AXP000003) from the same company. No further development found.

Phase I of intratumoral injection in 23 patients with recurrent head and neck cancer (Cancer Biol Ther 2009;8:676-82). Developer not identified from the sources consulted; often attributed to a Chinese biotech but not verified.

Given to patients in the Finnish Advanced Therapy Access Program (ATAP, 2007-2012), an individualised-treatment programme rather than a registered trial. Serotype 5 fibre version of the virus that became ONCOS-102 (Ad5/3).

platform: adenovirus (Ad5/3 chimera, E2F-1 promoter, Delta-24, GM-CSF-armed)
notes: ATAP construct (2007-2012). Sometimes given the code CGTG-602; the code was not verified here, so it is not listed as an alias.
ATAP construct (2007-2012).
ATAP construct (2007-2012); unarmed, replication controlled by a long cyclooxygenase-2 promoter.
ATAP construct (2007-2012), written Ad5/3-hTERT-CD40L in some reports and reported elsewhere under the code CGTG-401; the code was not verified here.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5/3 chimera, Delta-24, sodium iodide symporter-armed)
notes: ATAP construct (2007-2012); the NIS transgene allows imaging of virus spread by radioiodine uptake.
ATAP construct (2007-2012); a rare fully serotype-3 oncolytic adenovirus.

originator: University of Glasgow (MRC Institute of Virology)
notes: First engineered oncolytic HSV given to humans (glioma, Edinburgh/Glasgow, published 2000). Later sponsors Crusade Laboratories then Virttu Biologics; Virttu acquired by Sorrento Therapeutics 2017. No recent trials found; treated as discontinued.

Second-generation oHSV; first-in-human glioma trial 1998-2000 (Markert et al.). Paediatric trials run by the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the Pediatric Brain Tumor Consortium. A planned phase 2 (NCT04482933) was withdrawn.

Originally R7020, built as a live attenuated HSV vaccine candidate, later developed as an oncolytic for colorectal liver metastases by NeuroVir and MediGene (phase I/II by hepatic arterial infusion). Discontinued; the asset later passed to Catherex, acquired by Amgen in 2015 (deal not re-verified here).

Not genetically engineered: a spontaneously arising replication-competent mutant of HSV-1 strain HF. Dosed in Japan and the US (pancreatic cancer, head and neck cancer, melanoma). Development status after the phase II melanoma work not confirmed.
Chinese oncolytic HSV-1 armed with GM-CSF, built on a clinical isolate from a Han Chinese patient. Phase Ib in unresectable stage IIIC-IV melanoma published in J Immunother Cancer 2022.
RP2: the RP1 backbone with an added anti-CTLA-4 antibody-like molecule. Dosed with and without nivolumab; a phase 2 in colorectal cancer (NCT05733611) was terminated.
RP2 backbone with CD40L and 4-1BBL in place of GM-CSF, plus the anti-CTLA-4 molecule. First patient dosed in a phase 1 in 2021; phase 2 NCT05733611 terminated.
Also written MVR-T3011. Dosed intratumorally, intravenously and by hepatic arterial infusion in China, Australia and the US.

Glioma-directed oncolytic HSV-1 carrying IL-12 and an anti-PD-1 antibody; delivered into the brain (NCT06126744). Whether it is the same construct as T3011 with a different delivery device, or a distinct construct, is not fully clear from public sources; entered separately because it has its own NCIt concept and code.
Registered in China as 'recombinant human IL12/IL15-PDL1B oncolytic HSV-1 injection (Vero cell)'. Trials in hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic and gastric cancer.
Second Virogin oHSV: IL-12 and IL-15/IL-15Ralpha, without the PD-L1 blocking peptide of VG161; a distinct construct, so a separate program.
Attenuated by microRNA target cassettes rather than ICP34.5 deletion; carries five transgenes. Oncorus discontinued the programme in 2022 when it reprioritised to self-amplifying RNA.
Second-generation gamma34.5-deleted oHSV in which the human cytomegalovirus IRS1 gene restores late protein synthesis in tumour cells. Phase 1 in recurrent glioma (NCT03657576).

gamma34.5-deleted oHSV carrying human IL-12 (the murine counterpart is M002). Phase 1 in recurrent glioma (NCT02062827); a further phase 1 in diffuse midline glioma opened in 2025 (NCT07076498). No NCIt concept found for M032.

originator: Brigham and Women's Hospital (E. Antonio Chiocca)
notes: rQNestin34.5v.2: ICP34.5 restored but placed under the nestin promoter, so replication is limited to nestin-expressing glioma cells. Phase 1 with cyclophosphamide (NCT03152318); results in Nature 2023.

originator: Nationwide Children's Hospital / The Ohio State University
notes: ICP6 replaced by rat CYP2B1, which converts cyclophosphamide to its active metabolite. Phase 1 in primary and metastatic liver tumours (NCT01071941); dosing route and final enrolment not re-verified from a primary report.
Oncolytic HSV-2 armed with GM-CSF, the most clinically advanced HSV-2-based oncolytic. Dosed intratumorally in solid tumours and melanoma and intravesically in bladder cancer.
OH2 backbone armed with an anti-PD-L1/CD3 bispecific antibody instead of GM-CSF. A first-in-human phase I in cervical cancer is registered; dosing not confirmed from a primary report.

NCIt concept C200561 ('Oncolytic HSV-1 R130') with a Chinese trial registration; construct, originator and sponsor not established from public sources. Entered so the name resolves; needs curator checking.
Oncolytic HSV-1 in a phase 1 intratumoral study alone and with cetrelimab (NCT06311578, recruiting). Construct details not disclosed.

GLV-1h68/GL-ONC1, renamed Olvi-Vec and given the INN olvimulogene nanivacirepvec. Dosed intravenously, intraperitoneally and intrapleurally; phase 3 OnPrime (GOG-3076) in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer ongoing.

Armed with the yeast FCU1 gene, used with oral flucytosine. Licensed to Tasly Biopharmaceuticals for China, where it is called T601 (NCIt lists T601 as a synonym of TG6002), so T601 is recorded here as the same program and not a separate one.
Also coded TG6030. Armed with the BioInvent anti-CTLA-4 antibody 4-E03 and GM-CSF; phase I/IIa NCT04725331 terminated 2025.
Intravenous oncolytic vaccinia carrying IL-12 and a full-length anti-CTLA-4 antibody; phase 1 in NSCLC (NCT05788926) terminated 2025.

The 'double-deleted' vaccinia vvDD armed with cytosine deaminase and the somatostatin receptor; phase 1 by intratumoral and intravenous injection (NCT00574977). The unarmed vvDD backbone is a platform, not a separate program here. A cell-carrier form (autologous CIK cells loaded with vvDD-CDSR, CRX100, NCIt C179187) is a different product and is not entered.

Double-deleted vaccinia carrying a tumour-matrix-anchored human IL-2; phase 1 by intratumoral injection in gastrointestinal and peritoneal tumours (NCT07001592, recruiting since June 2025). Dosing of at least one patient inferred from the recruiting status, not confirmed by a report.

Trade-named VAXINIA. CF33 is a chimera assembled by co-infection with nine orthopoxviruses, so no single parent NCBI taxon is given. Phase 1 MAST study (NCT05346484) dosed patients intratumorally and intravenously; terminated January 2026.
Trade-named CHECKvacc. CF33 expressing hNIS and an anti-PD-L1 antibody; first-in-human intratumoral study in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (NCT05081492).
Trade-named onCARlytics: paints tumour cells with truncated CD19 so that anti-CD19 agents (blinatumomab, CAR-T) can act. First patient dosed in the phase 1 OASIS trial in October 2023.

Oncolytic vaccinia reported to carry IL-7 and IL-12; phase 1 intratumoral study with and without pembrolizumab completed April 2024 (NCT03954067). The transgene identities are from secondary sources and need checking.

Recombinant human IL-21-expressing oncolytic vaccinia virus injection; phase 1 in advanced solid tumours (NCT05914376, active) and a phase 2 in pancreatic cancer. Route not stated in the registration.
Also called RIVAL-01. Expresses Flt3 ligand, an anti-CTLA-4 antibody and IL-12; phase 1/2a with pembrolizumab (NCT04301011) terminated January 2023 and the programme dropped.
Oncolytic vaccinia from the Pfizer/Ignite collaboration; phase 1 with sasanlimab (NCT05061537) terminated October 2022. Construct and route not disclosed.
Vaccinia Enhanced Template platform virus expressing IL-12 and a TGF-beta inhibitor; phase 1/1b alone and with atezolizumab (NCT06444815, recruiting since June 2024).
Korean oncolytic vaccinia given with hydroxyurea; earlier phase 1 work in Korea and a phase 1 with hydroxyurea/atezolizumab (NCT07190833, recruiting). Construct details and route not confirmed.
Chinese oncolytic vaccinia; phase 1 intratumoral studies in advanced solid tumours (NCT06508307) and in recurrent glioma (NCT06660056). Construct not described in the registrations.
Recombinant oncolytic vaccinia virus injection; phase 1 in advanced refractory solid tumours (NCT07128914, recruiting since August 2025). Construct and route not described.
First-in-human phase 1 oncolytic vaccinia (NCT06910657, recruiting since April 2025). The related ViroMissile candidate IDOV-SAFE is a separate program on the same platform.

originator: Institute of Chemical Biology and Fundamental Medicine SB RAS
sponsor: Institute of Chemical Biology and Fundamental Medicine SB RAS
notes: Russian double-recombinant vaccinia carrying GM-CSF in the thymidine kinase locus and the milk protein fragment lactaptin in the growth-factor locus. Phase 1 (NCT05376527) first stage reported complete in October 2024.

Attenuated Edmonston-lineage measles virus engineered to express soluble CEA as a marker of viral gene expression. Dosed intraperitoneally in recurrent ovarian cancer (NCT00408590) and intratumorally/intracavitary in glioma; only the ovarian route is verified here.

Edmonston-lineage measles virus encoding the thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (SLC5A5) for imaging and radiovirotherapy. Separate construct from MV-CEA, tested separately in humans. Also given inside mesenchymal stromal cells in a separate delivery study (carrier, not a separate construct).
Edmonston-lineage measles virus encoding secreted Helicobacter pylori neutrophil-activating protein (NAP). Transgene is bacterial, so not an HGNC symbol.
Naturally attenuated, non-recombinant mesogenic NDV. Developed by Pro-Virus, which became Wellstat Biologics. Discontinued; no active trials found.

originator: United Cancer Research Institute (Laszlo K. Csatary)
notes: Attenuated NDV given to patients from the 1970s onward, largely outside conventional registered trials (case series and compassionate use); evidence base is weaker than for the other programs here. Reported routes include inhalation, which has no SPEC route value; intravenous recorded.
Lentogenic NDV HUJ strain; phase I/II in recurrent glioblastoma multiforme. Academic programme; no current sponsor found.
Recombinant NDV armed with GM-CSF (recNDV(GM-CSF)). Phase 1 with durvalumab completed 2022; no follow-on trial found, so presumed discontinued. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).

Recombinant VSV expressing human interferon beta and the sodium iodide symporter; brand/development name Voyager-V1 (VV1). Mayo Clinic and Vyriad both sponsor trials. The IFN-beta-only predecessor (NCT01628640) is a separate program, VSV-hIFNbeta. Transgenes moved from targets to virus.tsv (spec 0.2).

platform: VSV-GP (vesicular stomatitis virus with LCMV glycoprotein)
notes: Chimeric VSV whose G protein is replaced by the LCMV glycoprotein (VSV-GP), reducing neurotoxicity. Viratherapeutics was acquired by Boehringer Ingelheim in 2018. Given both intravenously and intratumorally in study 1456-0001.

Maraba MG1 (G protein Q242R, M protein L123W) encoding MAGE-A3, given as a boost after an adenoviral Ad-MAGEA3 prime. Ad-MAGEA3 is a separate adenoviral construct and belongs to the adenovirus group, not entered here. Turnstone deprioritised the MG1 programme; NCT03773744 was withdrawn.

Naturally occurring picornavirus with tropism for neuroendocrine tumours; development code NTX-010. Trials in small cell lung cancer and in paediatric neuroendocrine tumours. Discontinued; Neotropix no longer active.
Unmodified coxsackievirus A21, brand CAVATAK; renamed V937 after Merck acquired Viralytics in 2018. Merck has since stopped the programme. INN gebasaxturev.

Live attenuated Sabin type 1 poliovirus whose internal ribosome entry site is replaced by that of human rhinovirus type 2, removing neurovirulence. Given intratumorally, into glioma by convection-enhanced delivery.

originator: Augusts Kirhensteins Institute of Microbiology (Aina Muceniece)
notes: Non-genetically-modified ECHO-7 enterovirus adapted to melanoma. Registered in Latvia 2004; marketing authorisation suspended 30 May 2019 after batch potency failures. Reported registrations in Georgia, Armenia and Uzbekistan were not verified here. Efficacy evidence is widely regarded as inadequate.

Replication-competent retroviral vector (Toca 511) delivering optimised yeast cytosine deaminase, which converts the companion prodrug 5-fluorocytosine (Toca FC, extended-release flucytosine) to 5-FU. Toca FC is a small molecule and not a separate virus program. Phase 3 Toca 5 missed its overall survival endpoint in September 2019; Tocagen merged into Forte Biosciences in 2020 and the programme ended.

Wild-type rat protoparvovirus H-1, unmodified. ParvOryx01 in glioblastoma used intratumoral/intracerebral and intravenous/intracerebral arms; ParvOryx02 treated pancreatic carcinoma. The only non-adenovirus, non-herpes, non-pox DNA virus found dosed in humans as an oncolytic.

Recombinant oncolytic virus M1, a Getah-like alphavirus; phase 1 of intratumoral injection in advanced solid tumours (NCT06368921). Taxonomy assigned to Getah virus is the curator's best match and is not confirmed by the sponsor.

Engineered M1 variant given intravenously (NCT06046742); entered separately from VRT106 because the two were taken into humans as different agents by the same sponsor. Whether they are genuinely different constructs needs checking with the sponsor.

Hemagglutinating virus of Japan envelope: inactivated, replication-incompetent Sendai virus particles given intratumorally, development code GEN0101. Included because it is a virus particle therapy dosed as an intratumoral anti-tumour agent, but it does not replicate, so the owner may prefer to exclude it from an oncolytic census.

Historical: Egypt 101 isolate of West Nile virus inoculated into cancer patients in the early 1950s, among the first deliberate oncolytic virus studies in humans. A laboratory virus stock, not a developed product; entered for historical completeness.

Genetically engineered oncolytic VSV expressing the tumour antigen NY-ESO-1; first-in-human phase 1 NCT04787003 dosed 18 patients intratumorally (Hua et al., J Immunother Cancer 2025, PMID 40480657). Trial code C045. Commercial developer not named in the registration or the paper abstract; left empty.

Attenuated VSV engineered to encode a CD3/PD-L1 bispecific antibody, per the NCT07260591 registration. Compassionate-use/phase 1 study at the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinxiang Medical College, recruiting from December 2025; concurrent intravenous and intratumoral dosing. Attenuating mutations not described.

Named in NCT05644509 as 'vesicular stomatitis oncolytic virus injection (Revottack)', given intravenously with toripalimab at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University. Construct, transgenes and developer are not stated anywhere found; NCIt holds only a generic concept C199297 (Oncolytic Vesicular Stomatitis Virus) that also carries an unrelated YSCH-01 synonym, so no ncit code is recorded. Possibly the same product as another Chinese oncolytic VSV (RT-01, VSV-02, OVV-01): unresolved.

Second-generation oncolytic HSV-1 expressing an anti-PD-1 scFv-Fc, a TGF-beta receptor II decoy and IL-12 (NCIt C187651); development name Seprehvec, after Sorrento/Virttu's first-generation Seprehvir (HSV1716, AXP000073). Phase 1b NCT05361954 was registered in 2022 but still shows 'not yet recruiting'; Sorrento filed for bankruptcy in 2023, so whether any patient was dosed is unverified.

platform: vesicular stomatitis virus (Indiana serotype, human IFN-beta-armed)
notes: Recombinant VSV expressing human interferon beta WITHOUT the sodium iodide symporter, i.e. the construct preceding VSV-IFNbeta-NIS (AXP000119). NCIt keeps the two apart (C102545 vs C131580). Dosed intratumorally and intrahepatically in the completed Mayo phase 1 NCT01628640 (2012-2019) in hepatocellular carcinoma and other solid tumours.

Intravenously delivered oncolytic vaccinia virus of ViroMissile's IDOV (Intravenously Deliverable Oncolytic Virus) platform, reported by the company to carry an unusually high fraction of extracellular enveloped virions. Separate program from IDOV-Immune (AXP000110), ViroMissile's armed candidate; IDOV-SAFE is described as the company's first clinical-stage virus. Dosed in NCT06380309 (55 patients, pMMR/MSS colorectal cancer, Peking University Cancer Hospital) and in the CAMS platform study NCT06346041. Engineering and transgenes are not disclosed.

Engineered oncolytic HSV-1 carrying a cytosine deaminase (CD) gene, given with flucytosine (5-FC, listed as 'ONF') in recurrent malignant glioma: phase 1/2 NCT06562621 at Beijing Tiantan Hospital, shown as completed. Backbone deletions are not described in the registration.

originator: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine
sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine
notes: Oncolytic vaccinia virus delivering an anti-CD19 CAR in vivo (CAR-T/CAR-macrophage), phase 1 NCT07398963 in relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphoma, intratumoral and intravenous arms, recruiting from February 2026. Distinct from CF33-CD19 (AXP000101), which instead makes tumour cells express truncated CD19: here the virus delivers the receptor to host immune cells. Strain and deletions not described.
Historical: patients treated with mumps virus in Japan, reported by Asada in Cancer (1974), "Treatment of human cancer with mumps virus". Strain and routes not verified here.

platform: adenovirus (Ad5, E1 region replaced by a p53 expression cassette)
notes: First gene therapy approved anywhere: SFDA (now NMPA) licence 16 October 2003 for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, launched April 2004. Replication-defective Ad5 with the E1 region replaced by a wild-type human p53 cassette; promoter not verified. Distinct from contusugene ladenovec (AXP000142) and SCH-58500 (AXP000152), which are separate Ad-p53 constructs.

Advexin; reached phase 3 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. FDA told Introgen in 2008 that the BLA was not sufficiently complete to file; the company restructured and the programme stopped. Ad5CMV-p53 is the construct name.

FDA approved 16 December 2022 (BLA 125700) as Adstiladrin, the first gene therapy for bladder cancer; proper name nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg. Given intravesically with the polyamide surfactant Syn3, which is part of the product rather than a separate agent. Earlier codes SCH 721015 (Schering-Plough) and TR-002 (FKD Therapies).

CAN-2409: non-replicating Ad5 carrying herpes simplex virus thymidine kinase, injected into the tumour and followed by oral valacyclovir (the prodrug is a separate agent, not part of the program). Phase 3 in localised prostate cancer (ProstAtak) reported improved disease-free survival; also studied in glioma (GliAtak) and NSCLC. Virafir is a later brand name.

VB-111: non-replicating Ad5 in which a modified murine pre-proendothelin-1 promoter (PPE-1-3x, with a hypoxia-responsive element) drives a Fas-chimera transgene (TNFR1 extracellular and transmembrane domains fused to the Fas intracellular death domain), to kill angiogenic tumour endothelium. Given intravenously. Phase 3 OVAL in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer did not show benefit; earlier phase 3 in recurrent glioblastoma (GLOBE) also failed.

Intratumoral adenovirus carrying human IL-12 under the RheoSwitch Therapeutic System, switched on by the oral activator ligand veledimex (a separate agent). Phase 1/2 in recurrent glioblastoma and in breast cancer; INXN-2001 is the Intrexon code. The related product INXN-3001 (NCIt C101789) is autologous dendritic cells transduced with the same switch and is a different program, not entered here.

Cerepro: adenoviral HSV thymidine kinase injected into the wall of the resection cavity after surgery for high-grade glioma, followed by intravenous ganciclovir. The CHMP adopted a negative opinion and Ark withdrew the EU application on 8 March 2010 during re-examination; never approved. EG-009 is the development code.

Recombinant adenovirus encoding human endostatin, developed in China and studied intratumorally in head and neck cancer with chemotherapy. Endostatin is a fragment of collagen XVIII alpha-1 (COL18A1), recorded as the gene of origin. Highest phase not verified here.

Adenovirus encoding human interferon gamma, injected into skin tumours. Developed by Transgene as TG1042 for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, later taken forward by Ascend Biopharmaceuticals as ASN-002 for basal cell carcinoma (phase 2). Adenovirus serotype not verified.

TNFerade: adenovirus carrying human TNF-alpha under the radiation-inducible EGR1 promoter, injected into the tumour and combined with radiotherapy. Reached a phase 3 trial in locally advanced pancreatic cancer (NCT00051467) with 5-fluorouracil and radiation, which did not improve survival. Construct name ADGVEGR.TNF.11D.

Generx: single intracoronary infusion of a non-replicating Ad5 carrying human FGF-4 to induce collateral vessel growth in refractory angina due to coronary artery disease. Reached phase 3 (AFFIRM / AWARE); FDA cleared a further US phase 3 study. Not a cancer product.

Recombinant adenovirus-p53 from Canji/Schering-Plough, studied intraperitoneally in ovarian cancer and intratumorally in NSCLC in the late 1990s and early 2000s; no benefit shown and development stopped. A separate construct from Gendicine (AXP000141) and contusugene ladenovec (AXP000142). Also called ACN53.
Ad-mda7: adenovirus carrying melanoma differentiation-associated gene 7 (IL-24), injected intratumorally in phase 1 trials in melanoma and other solid tumours. Development stopped with Introgen.

Ad5 [E1-, E2b-] vector of the Etubics (now ImmunityBio) AdenoVerse-style platform, given subcutaneously; the E2b deletion is intended to allow repeat dosing despite pre-existing Ad5 immunity. Studied alone and in the multi-antigen Tri-Ad5 / 'Triad' regimens, which are combinations and not programs of their own. NCIt preferred name: Ad5 [E1-, E2b-]-CEA(6D) Vaccine.

Ad5 [E1-, E2b-] vector of the Etubics (now ImmunityBio) AdenoVerse-style platform, given subcutaneously; the E2b deletion is intended to allow repeat dosing despite pre-existing Ad5 immunity. Studied alone and in the multi-antigen Tri-Ad5 / 'Triad' regimens, which are combinations and not programs of their own. NCIt preferred name: Ad5 [E1-, E2b-]-HER2/neu Vaccine.

Ad5 [E1-, E2b-] vector of the Etubics (now ImmunityBio) AdenoVerse-style platform, given subcutaneously; the E2b deletion is intended to allow repeat dosing despite pre-existing Ad5 immunity. Studied alone and in the multi-antigen Tri-Ad5 / 'Triad' regimens, which are combinations and not programs of their own. NCIt preferred name: Adenoviral Brachyury Vaccine ETBX-051.

Ad5 [E1-, E2b-] vector of the Etubics (now ImmunityBio) AdenoVerse-style platform, given subcutaneously; the E2b deletion is intended to allow repeat dosing despite pre-existing Ad5 immunity. Studied alone and in the multi-antigen Tri-Ad5 / 'Triad' regimens, which are combinations and not programs of their own. NCIt preferred name: Adenoviral MUC1 Vaccine ETBX-061.

Ad5 [E1-, E2b-] vector of the Etubics (now ImmunityBio) AdenoVerse-style platform, given subcutaneously; the E2b deletion is intended to allow repeat dosing despite pre-existing Ad5 immunity. Studied alone and in the multi-antigen Tri-Ad5 / 'Triad' regimens, which are combinations and not programs of their own. NCIt preferred name: Adenoviral PSA Vaccine ETBX-071.

PRGN-2012: non-replicating gorilla adenovirus expressing HPV 6 and HPV 11 antigens, given as four subcutaneous injections over 12 weeks. FDA approved 14 August 2025 as Papzimeos (STN 125832, proper name zopapogene imadenovec-drba) for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis in adults: the first approved therapy for that disease, and a full rather than accelerated approval. A therapeutic vaccine against an HPV-driven benign neoplasm; recorded here as a cancer vaccine. The exact gorilla adenovirus serotype of the AdenoVerse vector is not stated in the sources used.

Gorilla adenovirus expressing HPV-16 and HPV-18 E6/E7 antigens with multiple cytotoxic T-cell epitopes; phase 1/2 in HPV-associated cancers, including with bintrafusp alfa and in recurrent oropharyngeal cancer. Separate construct from PRGN-2012 (AXP000159), which carries HPV 6/11.

GRT-C901: individualised neoantigen priming vaccine on a chimpanzee adenovirus vector, the adenoviral half of the GRANITE regimen (prime GRT-C901, boost the self-amplifying mRNA GRT-R902 / sapecmeran autogene, NCIt C156926, which is a separate non-viral program outside this pass). Phase 2/3 in metastatic colorectal cancer; Gritstone filed for bankruptcy protection in 2024. Vector usually described as ChAdV68, derived from chimpanzee adenovirus C68; serotype not verified from a primary source here.

Shared-neoantigen ('off the shelf') adenoviral priming vaccine of Gritstone's SLATE regimen, boosted by the self-amplifying mRNA GRT-R904 (NCIt C165515, outside this pass). Phase 1/2 in KRAS-mutant and other shared-neoantigen solid tumours. Distinct cassette from the individualised GRT-C901 (AXP000161), hence a separate program.

platform: great ape adenovirus (GAd20) prime with MVA boost
notes: Heterologous prime-boost of a great ape (gorilla) adenovirus GAd20-209-FSP prime and an MVA-209-FSP boost, both encoding 209 shared frameshift peptide neoantigens of microsatellite-unstable tumours. Marketed as one product, so entered as one program per spec section 1; the poxvirus boost is recorded here rather than as its own entry. Phase 1b/2 in Lynch syndrome carriers and in dMMR/MSI-high tumours with pembrolizumab. NCIt holds the two components separately (GAd-209-FSP C162805, MVA-209-FSP C162806), so no single NCIt code is recorded.

Adenovirus type 5 expressing human guanylyl cyclase C fused to the universal helper T-cell epitope PADRE; phase 1 in gastrointestinal cancers. An Ad5.F35 chimeric version has also been studied; vector details not verified beyond the NCIt record.

Adenovirus type 5 expressing MAGE-A3, used as the priming dose before the oncolytic MG1-MAGEA3 Maraba rhabdovirus boost (NCIt C118973, a separate oncolytic program). Phase 1/2 in MAGE-A3-positive solid tumours and NSCLC. The NCIt record 'MAGE-A3-expressing Adenovirus Type 5 Vaccine' (synonyms Adenovirus/MAGE-A3, AdMA3) does not name Turnstone, so the identification rests on the trial literature and should be checked.

platform: autologous dendritic cells transduced ex vivo with an adenoviral vector
notes: Autologous dendritic cells transduced outside the body with an adenovirus encoding tyrosinase, MART-1 and MAGE-A6 (AdVTMM2), then given back to the patient; phase 1 in melanoma. Entered as ex vivo gene transfer: the adenovirus modifies the cells rather than being administered itself.

AZD1222: replication-deficient chimpanzee adenovirus ChAdOx1 (derived from chimpanzee adenovirus Y25) encoding the full-length SARS-CoV-2 spike with a tPA leader. Two intramuscular doses. First authorised by the MHRA on 30 December 2020 and given conditional marketing authorisation in the EU on 29 January 2021 as Vaxzevria; licensed to the Serum Institute of India as Covishield and authorised in many other countries, which are not all listed here. AstraZeneca withdrew the EU authorisation in 2024 for commercial reasons (not verified from an agency source here). 'ChAdOx1' alone is the platform and is not listed as an alias.

Replication-incompetent E1-deleted Ad26 encoding a stabilised SARS-CoV-2 spike, made in PER.C6 cells; single intramuscular dose. FDA emergency use authorisation 27 February 2021, revoked June 2023 at the manufacturer's request; EU conditional marketing authorisation 11 March 2021, converted to standard on 9 January 2023 and withdrawn on 26 July 2024 for commercial reasons. UNII taken from the Wikipedia infobox and not from an FDA record.

originator: Beijing Institute of Biotechnology (Academy of Military Medical Sciences)
notes: Convidecia: single-dose recombinant Ad5 encoding the SARS-CoV-2 spike. Approved for limited military use in China on 25 June 2020 and for general use in February 2021; WHO emergency use listing May 2022; emergency authorisations in Mexico, Pakistan, Hungary, Chile, Malaysia, Indonesia and others not all listed here. The nebulised form Convidecia Air is the same construct given by oral inhalation, so it is a route rather than a new program (NMPA booster approval 4 September 2022); 'inhaled' is not a route value in the spec, so the route cell lists intramuscular only.

platform: human adenovirus 26 prime, human adenovirus 5 boost (non-replicating)
originator: Gamaleya Research Institute of Epidemiology and Microbiology
sponsor: Gamaleya Research Institute of Epidemiology and Microbiology
notes: Sputnik V: heterologous two-dose regimen, rAd26 encoding the full-length SARS-CoV-2 spike on day 0 and rAd5 encoding the same spike on day 21. Marketed as one product, so one program per spec section 1; virus.tsv records the first dose's Ad26 vector and the Ad5 boost is in modifications. Registered in Russia on 11 August 2020 (licence LP-006395), a conditional registration before phase 3 results; the freeze-dried Gam-COVID-Vac-Lyo received a separate certificate LP-006423 on 26 August 2020, and Gam-COVID-Vac-M covers adolescents. Authorised in many other countries, not all listed here.

originator: Gamaleya Research Institute of Epidemiology and Microbiology
sponsor: Gamaleya Research Institute of Epidemiology and Microbiology
notes: The first (rAd26) component of Gam-COVID-Vac alone, authorised in Russia as a separate single-dose product on 6 May 2021. Kept apart from AXP000170 because it is registered and marketed as its own product, but it is the same construct as that regimen's first dose: a candidate for merging if the registry decides route/regimen variants should not be split.

Zabdeno: recombinant Ad26 encoding the Zaire ebolavirus (Mayinga strain) glycoprotein, the priming dose of the two-dose Ad26.ZEBOV / MVA-BN-Filo (Mvabea) regimen; the MVA boost is a separate program for the poxvirus pass. Authorised in the EU under exceptional circumstances on 1 July 2020 for people aged 1 year and older; the European Commission withdrew the authorisation on 1 May 2026 at the holder's request, and the product was never marketed in the EU.

Recombinant replication-defective human adenovirus type 5 carrying the Ebola virus glycoprotein, developed with the Beijing Institute of Biotechnology; licensed in China in 2017, the country's first Ebola vaccine. Exact approval date, agency name and the Ebola strain used for the glycoprotein were not verified from the sources read.

targets: HIV-1 Env; HIV-1 Gag; HIV-1 Pol
notes: Ad26 vector delivering four mosaic HIV-1 immunogens, given as four injections over a year with a clade C and mosaic gp140 protein boost in the last two doses. The phase 3 Mosaico trial (HVTN 706) was stopped in January 2023 for lack of efficacy. The related phase 2b Imbokodo regimen (HVTN 705) used Ad26.Mos.HIV, a different antigen set, which did not reach phase 3 and is not entered.

Ad26 encoding a pre-fusion conformation-stabilised respiratory syncytial virus F protein. Reached phase 3 (EVERGREEN, NCT04908683) in adults aged 60 and over after about 80% efficacy in the phase 2b CYPRESS challenge-free trial; Johnson & Johnson discontinued the programme in 2023. Some trials combined the vector with recombinant preF protein in one regimen.

iNCOVACC: replication-deficient adenovirus-vectored vaccine encoding a pre-fusion stabilised SARS-CoV-2 spike, given as nasal drops. Constructs were designed at Washington University in St. Louis (where the vector is described as a chimpanzee adenovirus, ChAd-SARS-CoV-2-S); the Indian regulator granted restricted use in an emergency situation for adults, announced on 6 September 2022, both as a primary two-dose course and as a heterologous booster. The source read does not name the chimpanzee adenovirus serotype, so the strain cell is left empty.

Single-dose non-replicating gorilla (great ape) adenovirus vector encoding the SARS-CoV-2 spike. The COVITAR trial (NCT04791423) was a completed phase 2/3 study of 10,300 participants, so the program meets the phase 3 bar; never authorised. The vector is usually reported as GRAd32, which the source read does not confirm, so the strain cell is left empty.

PROSTVAC: vaccinia-PSA-TRICOM prime (rilimogene galvacirepvec, NCIt C38681, UNII 59WJ3TGA5K) followed by fowlpox-PSA-TRICOM boosts (rilimogene glafolivec, NCIt C29560, UNII 7PLH7RM47T); recorded as one program because it is one prime-boost product with a single combined INN pair and NCIt concept (C132990). unii left empty because the product has two. Phase 3 PROSPECT (1,297 men, mCRPC) stopped for futility at interim analysis, reported September 2017. PSA is KLK3; TRICOM = CD80 (B7.1), ICAM1, CD58 (LFA-3).

PANVAC-V (inalimarev, NCIt C29317) vaccinia prime plus PANVAC-F (falimarev, NCIt C29316) fowlpox boosts, both encoding CEA, MUC-1 and TRICOM; one program (one prime-boost product), so ncit left empty rather than pick one component concept. Phase 3 NCT00088660 (TBC-PAN-003) in metastatic pancreatic cancer after gemcitabine, sponsored by Therion Biologics; Therion wound down in 2006. NCIt lists 'PANVAC' also as a synonym of CV301 (AXP000143), which is the later MVA-BN-based remake: that alias is marked ambiguous.

MVA-BN-CV301 prime (NCIt C143059) with FPV-CV301 boosts (NCIt C141298), encoding CEA, MUC-1 and TRICOM: the PANVAC antigen cassette rebuilt on the non-replicating MVA-BN backbone, hence a separate program from PANVAC (AXP000142). Phase 1/2 in NSCLC and bladder cancer with checkpoint inhibitors (Bavarian Nordic-sponsored). Originator/sponsor taken from the MVA-BN naming in NCIt and Bavarian Nordic press coverage; not independently confirmed here.

TG4010: MVA encoding MUC1 and human IL-2, subcutaneous, in first-line advanced NSCLC with chemotherapy; randomised phase 2b (TIME) reported 2016. MVA strain lineage recorded as MVA; specific MVA stock not verified here.

TG4001: MVA encoding HPV-16 E6 and E7 plus human IL-2, for HPV16-positive cancers; phase 1b/2 and a randomised phase 2 with avelumab (missed its primary endpoint, reported 2024). Also carried the Roche codes RO5217790/R3484. E6/E7 are deleted/detoxified in some descriptions; modification detail not verified here.
Individualised MVA vaccine encoding patient-specific neoantigens selected with NEC's AI platform; phase 1/2 trials in head and neck and ovarian cancer (US, UK, France). Route not recorded here.

TroVax: MVA encoding the oncofetal antigen 5T4 (TPBG); trials in colorectal, renal and prostate cancer, including the phase 3 TRIST study in renal cell carcinoma (NCT00397345) - the phase 3 designation and result were not verified from a primary source in this pass. Also carries the Oxford BioMedica code OXB-301.

MVA-BN-Brachyury prime with FPV-Brachyury-TRICOM boosts (NCIt C148402), encoding brachyury (TBXT) and TRICOM; phase 1/2 at the NCI in chordoma and other solid tumours. NCIt also holds a separate earlier concept 'MVA Brachyury-TRICOM' (C116777) whose relationship to this construct is unclear; that name is listed as an ambiguous alias.
MVA-BN encoding a modified HER2 (ERBB2) antigen; early-phase trials in HER2-expressing cancers. Exact antigen construct (HER2 epitope string vs full-length) and current status not verified here.

MVA encoding wild-type human p53 (TP53); phase 1 trials at City of Hope, including with gemcitabine in recurrent ovarian cancer (NCT02275039, taken from trial listings, registry record not opened) and in refractory gastrointestinal cancers. Route not recorded here.

Replication-defective canarypox (ALVAC) vaccine encoding CEA (CEACAM5) with the costimulatory molecule B7.1 (CD80); early-phase NCI trials in CEA-expressing cancers, some with GM-CSF or chemotherapy. NCIt also holds a CEA(6D) epitope-modified variant (C29982) and plain ALVAC-CEA concepts (C1648, C2743); those are recorded as separate names here only where the construct matches. Originator (Virogenetics/Aventis Pasteur) and vCP code not verified in this pass.
Canarypox vector vCP2292 encoding NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B) with TRICOM; early-phase trials in NY-ESO-1-expressing cancers. Sponsor and phase not verified in this pass.

Recombinant vaccinia virus encoding HPV-16 and HPV-18 E6 and E7; used in therapeutic trials for cervical and vulval intraepithelial neoplasia since the 1990s and still used as a boost after DNA priming (e.g. the PVX7/pBI-11 regimen, NCIt C212077). Vaccinia strain (Wyeth) and the Cantab/Xenova originator attribution were not verified from a primary source in this pass; replication competence recorded as replicating on that basis and should be checked.

originator: Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social / Virolab
notes: MVA encoding the bovine papillomavirus E2 protein, injected locally into HPV-associated intraepithelial lesions (intrauterine in women, intraurethral in men, at the lesion base for vulvar/anal lesions). A phase 3 study of 1,356 patients in Mexico and Venezuela (2007-2012) reported 89.4% complete lesion elimination in women; the trial was largely uncontrolled and the paper's efficacy figures are internally inconsistent. Route recorded as topical/intralesional is not in the registry's route vocabulary, so route is left empty and described here.

Non-replicating MVA with an E5R deletion expressing human Flt3L (FLT3LG) and OX40L (TNFSF4), injected intratumorally alone or with pembrolizumab; phase 1 NCT05859074. Recorded as in_vivo_gene_transfer rather than vaccine_vector because it delivers immune-stimulatory ligands, not a tumour antigen; it is not oncolytic (MVA does not replicate in human cells).

Vyjuvek: topical gel of a replication-defective HSV-1 vector carrying two copies of COL7A1, for wounds of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. FDA approved 19 May 2023 (first redosable topical gene therapy), European Commission 23 April 2025, Japan (MHLW) September 2025. An eye-drop formulation for ocular DEB complications is the same product in a different formulation, so not a separate program.

Nebulised (inhaled) replication-defective HSV-1 vector delivering two copies of full-length CFTR, for cystic fibrosis regardless of genotype; phase 1 CORAL-1, NCT05504837. 'Inhaled' is not in the registry's route vocabulary, so route is left empty. NCIt concept 'inetagugene geperpavec' (C177071, UNII 7RJ7NSG7A0) is a Krystal HSV-1 INN whose product could not be matched to a code here, so no UNII is recorded.

Nebulised (inhaled) replication-defective HSV-1 vector delivering two copies of SERPINA1 (normal human alpha-1 antitrypsin), for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PI*ZZ); phase 1 SERPENTINE-1, NCT06049082, first patient dosed February 2024. Route left empty because 'inhaled' is not in the route vocabulary.

Replication-incompetent HSV-1 vector delivering human IL-12 and IL-2 to tumours; given intratumorally (phase 1 OPAL-1, NCT05970497) and by inhalation for lung tumours and pulmonary metastases (phase 1 KYANITE-1, NCT06228326). FDA fast track for both routes. Recorded as in_vivo_gene_transfer, not oncolytic: the vector does not replicate.

Redosable eye-drop HSV-1 gene therapy driving corneal/ocular surface expression of nerve growth factor (NGF) in neurotrophic keratitis; phase 1/2 EMERALD-1, NCT06999733, dosed twice weekly for 8 weeks. The press release does not name the vector explicitly; HSV-1 is Krystal's platform.

Topical replication-defective, non-integrating HSV-1 vector delivering functional human TGM1 for TGM1-deficient autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (lamellar ichthyosis); phase 1/2 first-in-human, placebo-controlled, 2e9 pfu per site. Current development status not established in this pass.

Intradermal replication-defective, non-integrating HSV-1 vector delivering two copies of COL3A1 to raise type III collagen in skin; phase 1 PEARL-1, NCT04540900, in aesthetic indications (lateral canthal lines, decollete wrinkles). Aesthetic rather than disease indication, but a human gene therapy in a registered trial, so in scope.

Replication-defective HSV-1 vector deleted for ICP4 and ICP27 (and lacking ICP22/ICP47 promoters) carrying human preproenkephalin (PENK) under a CMV IE promoter in both ICP4 loci; injected intradermally in the painful dermatome. Phase 1 dose escalation in 10 patients with intractable cancer pain, NCT00804076, sponsored by Diamyd Incorporated (Ann Neurol 2011, PMID 21796661). Later taken forward by Periphagen; that transfer was not verified here.

targets: Zaire ebolavirus GP; Sudan ebolavirus GP; Tai Forest ebolavirus NP; Marburg virus GP
notes: Mvabea: MVA-BN encoding Zaire ebolavirus (Mayinga) GP, Sudan ebolavirus (Gulu) GP, Tai Forest ebolavirus nucleoprotein and Marburg virus (Musoke) GP; the boost of the two-dose Zabdeno (Ad26.ZEBOV) / Mvabea regimen. EU marketing authorisation 1 July 2020 under exceptional circumstances; withdrawn 1 May 2026 at the holder's request. Route (intramuscular) not stated on the EPAR page opened, so left empty.

targets: HIV-1 CRF01_AE gp120; HIV-1 Gag; HIV-1 protease
notes: Canarypox vector vCP1521 carrying HIV-1 clade AE (92TH023) env gp120 anchored by a clade B LAI gp41 segment, plus clade B LAI gag and protease. Prime in the phase 3 RV144 trial in Thailand (>16,000 volunteers, US Army/Thai MoPH), boosted with the AIDSVAX B/E protein: 31.2% efficacy in the modified intent-to-treat analysis, reported 2009. The protein boost is a separate, non-viral product. Route (intramuscular) not confirmed from the pages opened.

targets: HIV-1 subtype C gp120; HIV-1 Gag; HIV-1 protease
notes: Canarypox vector vCP2438, the subtype C adaptation of vCP1521: clade C ZM96 env gp120 with a clade B LAI gp41 anchor, plus LAI gag and protease. Prime in HVTN 100 and the phase 2b/3 HVTN 702 (Uhambo) trial in South Africa (5,407 participants, NIAID), with MF59-adjuvanted bivalent subtype C gp120 protein; vaccinations stopped January 2020 for no efficacy. A different construct from vCP1521, so a separate program.

targets: RSV F; RSV G (A and B); RSV N; RSV M2-1
notes: MVA-BN encoding five RSV antigens: fusion protein F (RSV-A long), glycoprotein G of subtypes A (A2) and B, nucleoprotein N and transcription elongation factor M2-1 (A2). Single-dose phase 3 VANIR trial in >20,000 adults aged 60+ missed a co-primary endpoint (42.9% efficacy against disease with 3+ symptoms vs 59% with 2+), reported 22 July 2023; the programme was discontinued. Route not recorded here.

platform: vesicular stomatitis virus (Indiana, G-deleted, ZEBOV GP-bearing)
originator: Public Health Agency of Canada (National Microbiology Laboratory)
notes: Replication-competent rVSV whose own glycoprotein gene is replaced by the Zaire ebolavirus (Kikwit 1995) GP; marketed as Ervebo. EMA authorisation was conditional on 2019-11-11 and converted to a standard marketing authorisation on 2021-01-14. Licensed in several African countries after WHO prequalification (not recorded here for lack of an agency record opened). Merck development code V920 and the earlier NewLink code BPSC-1001 are widely used but were not confirmed on a page opened for this pass, so they are not listed as aliases.

targets: DENV-1 prM/E; DENV-2 prM/E; DENV-3 prM/E; DENV-4 prM/E
notes: Dengvaxia: four live chimeric viruses on the yellow fever 17D-204 backbone, each carrying the prM and E genes of one dengue serotype. Counted as a vector because the administered virus is YF 17D carrying foreign (dengue) antigens and the immunity sought is against dengue, not yellow fever. EU authorisation withdrawn at the holder's request on 2025-10-21; first approvals were in Mexico and other endemic countries from December 2015 (no agency record opened for those, so only the EMA and FDA rows are recorded). NCIt search for 'Dengvaxia' returned no concept.

Live chimeric virus: yellow fever 17D-204 backbone with the prM and E genes of JEV SA14-14-2. Same 'carries something foreign' reasoning as CYD-TDV. Single subcutaneous dose from 12 months of age. WHO-prequalified 2014-09-18 with the Thai FDA as national regulatory authority of record. Exact national approval dates were not found on an agency page; the Thai and Australian rows are dated 2012 from the launch press releases that state marketing authorisation had been granted.

Live recombinant Schwarz-strain measles virus with an extra transcription unit encoding the chikungunya structural polyprotein. Included because a phase 3 trial was authorised and run (Themis, Belgian sites); Merck, which acquired Themis in 2020, later dropped the chikungunya programme. Merck code V184.

originator: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
notes: Live recombinant NDV-LaSota displaying a HexaPro prefusion-stabilised SARS-CoV-2 spike anchored by the NDV F transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains. Authorised for emergency use in Mexico as Patria (COFEPRIS, June 2024). The same construct is made under licence by other manufacturers (ButanVac in Brazil, HXP-GPOVac in Thailand); treated as one program per SPEC section 1 and those names are flagged ambiguous. Avimex also developed an inactivated presentation; the clinical trials cited here used the live vaccine.

originator: Epeius Biotechnologies (Erlinda M. Gordon, Frederick L. Hall)
notes: Replication-incompetent MoMLV-based vector whose envelope carries a von Willebrand factor-derived collagen-binding peptide, delivering a cytocidal N-terminal-deletion (dominant-negative) human cyclin G1 construct; given by intravenous infusion. Renamed DeltaRex-G. Reported as approved for all solid tumours in the Philippines (accelerated approval, 2007); the approval year comes from secondary sources, not an agency record. Not an oncolytic virus: the vector does not replicate.

platform: gammaretroviral vector (MoMLV-derived) ex vivo, autologous CD34+ bone marrow cells
originator: San Raffaele Telethon Institute for Gene Therapy
notes: Autologous CD34+ bone-marrow cells transduced ex vivo with a replication-deficient MoMLV-derived gamma-retroviral vector (GSK3336223) carrying the human ADA cDNA; single intravenous infusion. EU marketing authorisation 2016-05-26, originally GSK, transferred to Orchard Therapeutics and then to Fondazione Telethon; still authorised. Development code GSK2696273.

platform: retroviral vector (SFCMM-3) ex vivo, allogeneic haploidentical donor T cells
notes: Allogeneic haploidentical donor T cells transduced with the retroviral vector SFCMM-3 Mut2 #48 to express the HSV-TK Mut2 suicide gene and a truncated LNGFR marker, given after haploidentical HSCT so that ganciclovir can switch the cells off if GvHD occurs. EU conditional authorisation 2016-08-18, withdrawn 2019-10-09 at the holder's request for commercial reasons. The EMA and HAS documents say only 'retroviral vector'; the gammaretroviral (MLV-derived) backbone is not stated in the sources opened for this pass.

Propagation-defective Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus replicon packaged as virus-like replicon particles encoding CEA(6D); intramuscular. Phase 1/2 in advanced CEA-expressing cancer (NCT00529984, PMID 20679728). Included as a cancer vaccine, which this pass admits at any phase.

Virus-like replicon particles encoding the HER2 extracellular and transmembrane domains (HER2 ECD+TM); single-cycle alphavirus replicon with three of seven viral genes replaced by the insert. Phase 1 in HER2-overexpressing advanced cancer (NCT01526473). The alphavirus species is not named in the trial description; VEE is taken from the shared AlphaVax VRP platform and the NCIt concept.

Cocktail of six Escherichia coli phages, each carrying a CRISPR-Cas3 cassette that cuts the E. coli genome. Phase 1b NCT04191148 dosed it by intraurethral instillation; the phase 2 ELIMINATE trial NCT05488340 gives intraurethral plus intravenous doses. Target bacterium is not an HGNC symbol, so targets is empty.

Four E. coli phages armed with a CRISPR-Cas payload, given orally to reduce gut E. coli in haematological cancer patients at risk of bloodstream infection. Phase 1 NCT05277350 in healthy volunteers; phase 1b/2a NCT06938867 in patients before allogeneic HSCT.

Inhaled phage cocktail against Pseudomonas aeruginosa in cystic fibrosis. Phase 1b/2a NCT05010577 completed; phase 2b NCT06998043 under way. BX004-A is the drug product tested in the phase 1b/2a trial.

Personalised anti-Staphylococcus aureus phage treatment for diabetic foot osteomyelitis, matched to the patient's isolate from the PhageBank collection. Developed by Adaptive Phage Therapeutics, which BiomX acquired in March 2024; the phase 2 DANCE trial NCT05177107 (APT.DFI.001) is the trial BiomX reported as positive BX211 topline data in March 2025, so BX211 and the APT DFO product are one program, not two. Route not taken from a primary source yet, so left empty. PhageBank itself is a platform (SPEC section 1), not a program.

Topical anti-Staphylococcus aureus phage cocktail for atopic dermatitis. Its registered phase 1b/2a trial NCT05240300 was withdrawn, so the product has a registered trial but no published human use; kept on the registered-trial limb of the scope rule and flagged here.

Inhaled multi-phage product against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Phase 1b/2a SWARM-P.a. NCT04596319 in cystic fibrosis; phase 2 Tailwind NCT05616221 (AP-PA02-201) in non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis. A later product than AB-PA01 and entered separately.
Intravenous multi-phage product against Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia. Phase 1b/2a diSArm NCT05184764, topline reported 2025. A later product than AB-SA01 and entered separately.

Fixed-composition product of three obligately lytic myoviruses related to Staphylococcus phage K (Lehman 2019, Viruses 11:88). Given intravenously to 13 patients with severe S. aureus infection in an open single-arm study (Petrovic Fabijan 2020, Nat Microbiol 5:465-472) and in Australian compassionate cases; US expanded-access record NCT03395769. AmpliPhi Biosciences was renamed Armata Pharmaceuticals in 2019. virus_family is given as Herelleviridae because phage K is a Kayvirus of that family; the source itself says only 'myoviruses related to phage K'.

Anti-Pseudomonas aeruginosa phage product used under emergency/compassionate access, including three lung transplant recipients (Aslam 2019, Am J Transplant 19:2631-2639) and a ventilator-associated pneumonia case given it intravenously and by inhalation; US expanded-access record NCT03395743. Distinct from the later AP-PA02.

Topical phage cocktail for diabetic foot ulcers and infection, covering Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus and Acinetobacter baumannii. Phase 1/2a NCT04803708 (published) and phase 2 NCT05948592, both completed.
Oral phage preparation against adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) in Crohn's disease. Phase 1/2a NCT03808103 with Mount Sinai and Johns Hopkins.
Oral phage preparation against Shigella, tested in a human challenge model of shigellosis with Shigella flexneri 2a (phase 1/2a NCT05182749).
Oral phage cocktail against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, in healthy and VRE-colonised subjects (phase 1/2a NCT05715619, suspended).

Cocktail of 12 natural lytic anti-Pseudomonas aeruginosa phages, applied to burn wounds in the PhagoBurn trial NCT02116010 (Jault 2019, Lancet Infect Dis). PhagoBurn also had an anti-E. coli arm whose product name is not given in the sources seen, so no program was created for it. Pherecydes Pharma merged with Erytech in 2023 to form Phaxiam Therapeutics.

Anti-Staphylococcus aureus phage, supplied as a solution for injection and used with PP1815 under French compassionate access (ANSM) for bone and joint infection, intravenously for bacteraemia and endocarditis and by aerosol for purulent bronchopathy, and in the PhagoDAIR I trial NCT05369104 (EudraCT 2021-004469-11) and PhagoDAIR II NCT06605651. Entered separately from PP1815 because the two are separate injectable products that a phagogram can find active singly or together.

Anti-Staphylococcus aureus phage, solution for injection, used alongside PP1493 under French compassionate access and in PhagoDAIR I NCT05369104 and PhagoDAIR II NCT06605651. See PP1493 for why the two are separate programs.

Anti-Staphylococcus aureus phage preparation and, as of late 2024, the only phage medicine with a marketing authorisation in the EU, registered in Slovakia. No approvals row yet: no primary agency record giving the authorisation date was found, and the spec requires a date. Open question for Chase. virus_family given as Herelleviridae on the Kayvirus description in the Stafal literature. Route not taken from a label and left empty.

Anti-Pseudomonas aeruginosa phage product for ventilator-associated pneumonia; the registration calls it the component of the TP-122 cocktail and tests TP-122A itself (phase 1/2a NCT06370598). Separate program from TP-102, which is a different cocktail for a different indication.
Phage preparation tested topically in venous leg ulcers in a randomised double-blind phase 1 trial, NCT00663091. Originator not taken from a primary source, so left empty.
Phage preparation against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa for infected surgical wounds; phase 1/2a NCT06319235.

originator: Walter Reed Army Institute of Research
sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
notes: Anti-Pseudomonas aeruginosa phage cocktail made at the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research, given as a single dose in a phase 1b/2 trial in cystic fibrosis (NCT05453578, completed).
Anti-Pseudomonas aeruginosa phage product in a phase 1 trial in acute P. aeruginosa pneumonia (NCT07492771).
Phage preparation in a phase 1 trial in acute alcohol-associated hepatitis (NCT06750588), where the target is a cytolysin-producing gut bacterium rather than a wound or lung pathogen.
Bacteriophage-loaded microcapsule spray for colonised pressure injuries (S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, K. pneumoniae); phase 1/2a NCT04815798. The registration also calls it PL-03-BM.

Phage cocktail sprayed on second-degree burn wounds; phase 1 NCT04323475, where it is called both 'phage cocktail-SPK' and PGX-0100. Separate from BACTELIDE, the same company's pressure-injury product.
Achromobacter-targeting phage cocktail in a phase 1 pilot trial in people with cystic fibrosis and chronic Achromobacter lung infection (NCT07275905).
Phage cocktail against Mycobacterium abscessus subsp. abscessus pulmonary infection; phase 1 NCT07429162. Manufacturer not taken from a primary source.

Five-phage cocktail against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, used with DP-QB-STA-005 in a phase 2/3 feasibility trial in periprosthetic joint infection treated by DAIR (NCT07698002). Manufacturer not taken from a primary source.
Five-phage cocktail against Staphylococcus aureus, used with DP-QB-PSA-005 in the phase 2/3 periprosthetic joint infection trial NCT07698002.

originator: Eliava Institute of Bacteriophage, Microbiology and Virology
sponsor: Eliava Institute of Bacteriophage, Microbiology and Virology
notes: Long-marketed Georgian polyvalent phage cocktail (Pyo bacteriophage). Tested against placebo and antibiotics in a randomised trial of urinary tract infection in men undergoing transurethral prostate resection (NCT03140085), where it was instilled into the bladder. The commercial cocktail's composition is adjusted over time, which the registry records as one program.

Orally given T4-like coliphage preparation tested in Bangladeshi children with E. coli diarrhoea (NCT00937274, terminated; published 2016). The trial compared a Nestlé-made cocktail with a commercial Russian T4 preparation; this program is the Nestlé cocktail.

Lytic mycobacteriophage used therapeutically against Mycobacterium abscessus. First human use in 2019 as one of a three-phage cocktail with engineered derivatives of BPs and ZoeJ, given intravenously to a cystic fibrosis patient after lung transplantation (Dedrick 2019, Nat Med 25:730-733); now in a registered open-label individual-patient study as Muddy_HRMN0052 (NCT07228702). The engineered companions BPsDelta33HTH_HRM10 and ZoeJDelta45 are not entered as programs of their own yet; split them out if Chase wants the cocktail's components tracked separately.

Quality-controlled cocktail of Pseudomonas aeruginosa phages 14/1 and PNM and Staphylococcus aureus phage ISP, made at the Queen Astrid Military Hospital in Brussels with the Eliava Institute and applied to colonised burn wounds in a small clinical trial (nine patients, ten applications).

First gene therapy authorised in the EU (Glybera, 2012), for familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency. The authorisation expired on 28 October 2017 after uniQure chose not to apply for renewal, citing lack of demand; recorded as withdrawn, the nearest status the spec offers.

Subretinal AAV2 gene therapy for biallelic RPE65 mutation-associated retinal dystrophy; the first in vivo gene therapy licensed in the US. The FDA page lists approval letters dated 2017-12-19 and 2022-06-08 without saying which is the original, so the earliest is taken as the approval.

AAV9 gene replacement for 5q spinal muscular atrophy. One program covering both formulations: the intravenous one (Zolgensma, onasemnogene abeparvovec-xioi, FDA 2019) and the intrathecal one (Itvisma, onasemnogene abeparvovec-brve, FDA 2025-11, for patients 2 years and older). SPEC section 1 says a new route or formulation of the same construct is not a new program, so they share this ID and have an approval row each; the FDA's four-letter suffixes differ but the INN does not. The EU authorisation was conditional in 2020 and became full on 2022-05-17.

AAV2 vector carrying the DDC gene, infused into the putamen (two infusions per putamen) for aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase deficiency. Recorded with route `intracerebral`, the spec's nearest value for an intraputaminal infusion. Upstaza in the EU, Kebilidi in the US, one program. The EU authorisation was granted under exceptional circumstances.

AAV5 vector carrying a B-domain-deleted factor VIII gene for severe haemophilia A, given as a single intravenous infusion. EU authorisation is conditional; the US label requires no factor VIII inhibitors and no detectable anti-AAV5 antibodies.

AAV5 vector carrying a codon-optimised factor IX Padua (R338L) cDNA under the liver-specific LP1 promoter, for haemophilia B. US label restricts use to patients with a pre-existing neutralising anti-AAV5 titre below 1:700.

AAVrh74 vector with the MHCK7 promoter delivering a micro-dystrophin transgene for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Accelerated approval 2023-06-22 for ambulatory patients aged 4-5; a 2024-06-20 supplement extended it to patients 4 and older. Development code SRP-9001.

Recombinant AAVRh74var capsid carrying the factor IX Padua (R338L) variant for haemophilia B. Approved in the US as Beqvez (2024-04-25) and in the EU as Durveqtix (conditional, 2024-07-24); the EU authorisation was withdrawn at Pfizer's request on 2025-05-15 for commercial reasons and the product was never marketed there. The capsid is the label's AAVRh74var, not the AAV-Spark100 name used in earlier literature.

platform: AAV vector (capsid not stated in the sources seen)
notes: China's first approved rAAV gene therapy and its first for a rare disease: an AAV vector delivering an optimised factor IX gene to hepatocytes, approved by the NMPA in April 2025 for adults with moderate to severe haemophilia B, with Takeda China commercialising it. Approved in Macao in March 2026. Brand name XinJiuning. The capsid serotype is not given in the sources seen, so `strain` is empty.
